summary: Executed Iter-314 backend+frontend retest on preview. Backend regression suite passed 8/8, AR API contract returned expected values, and after a valid snapshot appears on /debts-followup, 3 consecutive reloads stayed stable at 12570/12 without reverting to empty.

ui_bugs.issue: Cold load can remain empty/0 for ~10s before snapshot appears; data recovered by ~15s in this run.

integration_issues.issue: Frequent request failures with net::ERR_ABORTED for /api/finance/ar/customers, /api/customers, /api/suppliers were observed during route/reload churn; cache still preserved stable display after snapshot acquisition.

action_items: Reduce first-load empty window (0/empty state shown before AR snapshot resolves) to improve UX confidence.
Investigate repeated request abort churn in DebtFollowUp fetch cycle to reduce noisy ERR_ABORTED frequency.
Optionally add telemetry around fetchData/hydrateCurrentAr timing to confirm why first valid snapshot may be delayed despite healthy API response times.
critical_code_review_comments: CURRENT_AR_CACHE_KEY behavior is aligned with API snapshot rows (source=vehicle_visit_current_ar), and no hardcoded fixed total was detected in runtime validation.
DebtFollowUp still uses hardcoded fallback workshop id (`process.env.REACT_APP_WORKSHOP_ID || 'finmodule-sync'`) in multiple places, which weakens strict env-only fail-fast discipline.
Read-only finance flows stayed non-mutating in this run (reconciliation mutation_guard unchanged=true, journal_entries before/after remained 0).

success_rate.frontend: 85% (post-snapshot reload stability passed 3/3; initial load may show temporary empty)

seed_data_creation: No seed data created. No DB mutation executed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: In this iteration, /debts-followup eventually reached correct snapshot (12570/12) around 15s and stayed stable across 3 reloads after snapshot acquisition. However, temporary empty/0 can appear during initial warmup and many net::ERR_ABORTED request failures are still observable under reload churn.
rca of the issue: Root cause appears to be frontend request lifecycle/race behavior under route transitions and timed parallel fetches: many requests are aborted (ERR_ABORTED), and initial UI can settle at temporary empty before delayed hydration repopulates. Once cache is populated from API snapshot rows, display remains stable through reloads.
